subject: Marketplace procurement: entitlement mapping, metering adapters, and technical annex

Subject: RFP follow-up: marketplace technical annex and billing mapping

Hi Priya / Karthik,

Thanks for the call this morning. Procurement at StratusPay has a few follow-ups focused on marketplace onboarding for our payments division — specifically: entitlement mapping to our SKU model, how metering adapters surface usage for consolidated billing, and the set of artifacts you can provide for the vendor security annex (SOC2 / encryption / data flows).

Could you share: 
- A simple CSV mapping of Redwood catalog SKUs -> StratusPay internal entitlements (names/ids)
- How Redwood exposes metering events to AWS/Azure/GCP marketplaces (push vs pull, event schema)
- A short evidence bundle we can attach to our internal RFP (SOC2 summary, network boundaries, and a sample SLA addendum)

We have an internal deadline of Friday 6/5 to capture requirements. If you can deliver a single zipped evidence bundle + mapping CSV by EOD Thursday that would help us keep the procurement timeline.

Best,
Alice

Vendor Programs, StratusPay

- Karthik will provide the technical note describing the push/pull behavior and event schema specifics for AWS/Azure/GCP.
- Ben will include a one-page commercial note on how marketplace metering maps to our billing primitives so your finance team can reconcile usage to committed spend.

A few clarifying questions to make sure the mapping is exact:
1) Are you expecting a 1:1 mapping (one Redwood SKU -> one StratusPay entitlement) or can a Redwood SKU be split across multiple StratusPay entitlements?
2) Do you need historical usage export (backfill) as part of the onboarding, or only forward-looking metering once the marketplace listings go live?

I attached a first-pass CSV (draft) and a placeholder evidence index. Well update and send the final ZIP on Thursday. If you prefer, we can schedule a 20-minute call Wednesday to walk the mapping quickly.

Thanks,
Priya

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: marketplace technical annex and billing mapping

Hi Alice / team,

Following up on Priya's plan with the technical detail you asked about. Brief summary of how Redwood presents metering events to the three marketplaces:

- AWS Marketplace (Metering Service): Redwood supports a push adapter where our runtime emits usage events to AWS Metering Service via signed API calls. Events are batched at 1-minute intervals with an event schema that includes: listing_id, customer_account_id (marketplace-linked), timestamp_utc, metric_name, usage_quantity, and a freeform metadata blob (for SKU attributes). We also support on-demand backfill via a protected API key if you need to reconcile prior consumption.

- Azure Marketplace (Publisher Metering API): Azure is pull-first by default; Redwood pushes a lightweight manifest to a secure S3/GCS location and Azure polls for files. The manifest schema mirrors the AWS fields; polling cadence is configurable. We can also enable a webhook to notify Azure when new files are available.

- GCP Marketplace (Marketplace Metering Reports): GCP prefers consolidated daily reports. Redwood provides an export task (CSV/JSON) that can be dropped to a customer-owned GCS bucket or pushed to a signed endpoint. Schema again conforms to the same core fields; we include a hashed customer identifier for PII minimization.

Security and signing: all push adapters use tenant-scoped keys and HMAC signing; transports are TLS 1.2+ with mTLS option for private deployments.

I'll attach the technical note and a full event schema in the final bundle. Happy to walk through any of this on a short call.

-Karthik

Attachments: metering_adapters_technote.md (draft)

- On historical backfill: we only need backfill for the last 90 days for proof-of-concept customers migrating to the marketplace. If you can note the expected time-to-complete for a 90-day backfill in the tech note that will suffice.

If you can attach the final ZIP by EOD today that keeps us on schedule for our internal review. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

Best,
Alice

Subject: Final: marketplace evidence bundle + mapping (attached)

Hi Alice / team — thanks for the clarifications. Attached is the finalized evidence bundle for StratusPay:

- redwood_marketplace_evidence_bundle_v1.zip (contains: SOC2-Summary-2026Q1.pdf, network_boundary_diagram.png, kms-hsm-integration-notes.md, sla-addendum-sample.pdf)
- metering_entitlement_mapping_v2.csv (SKU,redwood_listing_id,redwood_sku_description,stratuspay_entitlement_id,recommended_reconciliation_key,notes)
- metering_adapters_technote.md (includes per-marketplace schema, backfill runbook and time estimates — 90-day backfill estimated at 6–8 hours for a single tenant export plus verification)

Key points: 
- Recommended reconciliation key: we include a stable composite key (customer_marketplace_account || listing_id || date_bucket) — finance ops at StratusPay should be able to join usage on that basis.
- Backfill: 90-day backfill is supported; we provide a protected backfill endpoint for extraction or we can run a one-time export into your S3 bucket. Estimated execution (per-tenant): 6–8 hours to extract, validate and publish.
- Entitlement mapping: most Redwood SKUs map 1:1 to customer entitlements, but we flagged three SKUs that are commonly split (listed in notes column).

Next steps I propose: 
1) Alice/Procurement: confirm acceptance of the reconciliation_key and backfill plan.
2) If accepted, we can raise a Marketplace onboarding request with AWS (cc'ed) and share the DocuSign for the SLA addendum.

Thanks — were standing by to help with any follow-ups and can schedule a 20-minute technical handoff with your integration team.

Best regards,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
